_comment: Web-client demo catalog.  Each entry names an EXISTING .buda flow; the
server (src/web/demos.py) derives everything else from that file, so a
demo cannot drift from the flow it claims to be:
setup  — the commands above the first pipeline stage (shown in the
command box and run by 'Run commands'),
stages — the flow's OWN spelling of each pipeline stage, so the stage
buttons drive a hier flow with run_hier_bundler / hier planner,
flow   — the whole pipeline tail, which the 'Run flow' button replays
minus the commands that make no sense in a browser (visualize*,
Add a demo by adding an entry here — no server change.  A flow whose
require_file inputs are missing is listed as unavailable with its own
hint rather than failing when clicked.

demos.label: Flat — b44 bus (3 blocks, 52 bits)
demos.note: The starter: one fat bus, a rich candidate pool to step through.

demos.label: Hierarchical — multi-pin stress (35 buses, depth 2)
demos.note: Hierarchy-aware flow: cell-local templates + cross-level bundles.

demos.label: User guide — 2 blocks, 1 bus + 1 net
demos.note: The smallest end-to-end design; pairs with docs/USER_GUIDE.md.

demos.label: Comprehensive — 6 layers, mixed buses + checks
demos.note: Six-layer stack, several bus shapes, check_design + report_wl.

demos.label: Congestion — three buses competing for one channel
demos.note: Per-bundle generation; watch the planner spread the load.

demos.label: Keep-outs — routing around blocked regions
demos.note: Keep-out zones as hard constraints through to detailed NUTS.

demos.label: Channel stress — 16 blocks, post-NUTS replan + negotiate
demos.note: A healer flow: post_nuts layer reassignment then negotiate_congestion.

demos.label: RV SoC — imported DEF/LEF/Verilog (1230 nets, depth 4)
demos.note: A real imported design end to end; the full flow runs ~15s.
